CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for annual exam. It has been one year since last visit. Patient reports good compliance with exercise regimen including walking and yoga, which has significantly helped her arthritis. She denies joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups over the past year. She continues methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly without issues. Regarding atrial fibrillation, patient reports ongoing palpitations with the most recent episode occurring approximately one week ago. She has noticed palpitations tend to flare up with stress. She has been attempting meditation and exercise to manage stress with limited effectiveness. Patient reports event monitor was performed last month. Regarding reflux, patient has made dietary modifications including eliminating soda and reports no flare-ups in over five months. Protonix has been helpful.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses palpitations and nasal congestion related to allergies. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
Atrial fibrillation
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
Protonix 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly including walking and yoga. Exercises with her dog.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Heart rate well-controlled and regular. General: Well-appearing. Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, consistent with prior exams. Regular rate and rhythm at this time. Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally. Extremities: Edema and erythema noted on right elbow with pain to palpation. No lower extremity edema noted.

RESULTS
Event monitor: Shows patient in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pause pattern, transitioning from a-fib to regular rhythm.
Autoimmune panel: Within normal limits, indicating well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis on current methotrexate therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill ordered. Rheumatology referral available if needed.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Refer to cardiology for cardiac ablation to maintain normal sinus rhythm given episodic a-fib presentation.
3. Reflux: Continue protonix 40 mg daily. Continue dietary modifications avoiding coffee and spicy foods. Patient to report any additional issues.
